column3: <URL regex the rule must not be applied to>

column1: # Lines starting with `#` are comments. Plugin ids: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# OUTOFSCOPE is the narrow form: the rule stays live everywhere but the
# matching URLs, so a finding in our own code still fails the scan.
# The scan fails on any alert not listed here (fail_action: true), so this
# file is the DAST counterpart of .github/trivy-allowlist: every entry names
# the alert it accepts and why the finding is not exploitable in Turbo EA's
# deployment shape, and every entry is re-read at the quarterly allowlist
# review. Prefer fixing over listing — a missing header is a one-line nginx
# change. Never IGNORE a High-risk alert; downgrade it to WARN at most, with
# the mitigation written next to it.
# Seeded from the first dispatch run (2026-09-30, run 36746175997): 0 FAIL,
# 7 WARN. One of the seven was fixed at the source instead of listed here —
# 10036 (Server header leaked the nginx version: `server_tokens off`). The
# CSP rule (10055) had three findings; `frame-ancestors` was added to the app
# and /api policies, and the two that remain are accepted below. The rest
# are informational or not applicable to this deployment shape; each is Low
# or Informational risk in ZAP's own rating.
# A rule id covers every sub-alert of that plugin: zap-baseline's rules file
# keys on the plugin id, not on the alert reference (10055-4, 10055-6), so an
# IGNORE here is broad by construction. Where that matters — the CSP — the
# policy is pinned statically in backend/tests/services/test_nginx_headers.py
# so the accepted findings cannot widen into a script-src regression.
# CSP: Wildcard Directive (10055-4) and style-src unsafe-inline (10055-6).
# Medium in ZAP's rating, both deliberate. `img-src` allows `https:` because
# the Extension Store renders logos from the catalogue's own host and an
# extension page may show images from its vendor — an image cannot run
# script, and every scriptable directive stays 'self'. `style-src
# 'unsafe-inline'` is what MUI's Emotion runtime needs to inject its
# stylesheets; there is no 'unsafe-inline' on script-src anywhere. Both
# sub-alerts fire on every SPA page, so the plugin has to be listed; the
# static test keeps `script-src 'self'` exact on the app and embed policies.
# Reviewed 2026-09-30; revisit if Emotion nonces are adopted.

column3: img-src https: is deliberate (store logos, extension pages); style-src unsafe-inline is Emotion; script-src pinned by test_nginx_headers.py

column1: # Non-Storable Content. Informational. The API answers with
# Cache-Control: no-store on purpose — session-bound JSON must never land in a
# shared cache — and ZAP reports exactly that. Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: API responses are deliberately no-store; informational

column1: # Timestamp Disclosure - Unix. Low. The one hit is a 10-digit integer constant
# inside the minified SPA bundle (a library's epoch constant), not a leaked
# server time. Reviewed 2026-09-30; re-check if the hit moves to an API route.

column3: integer constant in the minified bundle, not a server timestamp

column1: # Modern Web Application. Informational. States that the site is a
# JavaScript application and the classic spider will see little; it is, and
# that is why the AJAX spider runs. Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: informational: it is an SPA, the AJAX spider is on

column1: # Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing. Medium in ZAP's rating, not
# actionable here: the only cross-origin <link> tags are the Google Fonts
# stylesheets (Material Symbols, Inter), whose CSS is generated per user
# agent, so no integrity hash can be pinned. font-src / style-src in the CSP
# restrict those origins to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com.
# Reviewed 2026-09-30; drops out if the fonts are ever self-hosted.

column3: Google Fonts stylesheets cannot carry an SRI hash; origins are CSP-pinned

column1: # Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy Header Missing. Low. COEP require-corp would
# refuse every cross-origin subresource that lacks CORP headers (the fonts
# above, the DrawIO assets) and pairs with COOP, which `location /` must
# never carry: the SSO popup relays its result to window.opener (#1126).
# Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: COEP would break fonts and the SSO popup relay; COOP is off by design

column1: # jgraph/drawio v31.4.1 is vendored into the frontend image and served under
# /drawio/. Five content rules fire on its own files — the minified bundles
# (app.min.js, main.js, extensions.min.js), the AsciiMath library and the
# dia.txt translation strings — none of which Turbo EA authors or can change
# short of forking DrawIO. OUTOFSCOPE keeps each rule live for the app's own
# bundle and skips only that path; a global IGNORE would hide the same
# finding in code that is ours. The two header alerts the same crawl raised
# on /drawio/ (10021, 10063) were fixed in the edge nginx config instead and
# are pinned by test_nginx_headers.py. The crawl is not deterministic: the
# first three runs never reached the editor, so this section was added on
# the fourth (2026-09-30, run 36770264921). Revisit on a DrawIO bump.
